title: conntrack-eviction-cascade-postmortem-draft
content:
Summary:

On 2024-11-07 we experienced a production incident affecting the inference-hosting cluster in us-west-2. The incident manifested as a cascade of pod evictions across multiple node pools over ~45 minutes and intermittent request failures for customer traffic. Root cause was conntrack table exhaustion on worker nodes (net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max reached) combined with delayed control-plane reactions due to elevated etcd write latency during an automated snapshot job. The conntrack exhaustion was triggered by a burst of short-lived upstream TCP connections from a misconfigured load-test job in the CI namespace + ephemeral client retries from a noisy internal health-check.

Impact:
- ~22% of replicas for the hosted-api deployment experienced transient Pod evictions and restarts, causing a 3–8s P99 latency spike and ~4.3% increase in 5xx on customer traffic for 37 minutes.
- Several internal jobs (batch workers) went into CrashLoopBackOff due to connection failures.
- No customer data loss; graceful restarts handled in most cases, but increased tail latency and error budget burn.

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 2024-11-07 02:09: Alert: high 5xx rate for hosted-api (Alert: api-5xx-rate > 1.5%) routed to oncall.
- 02:12: Pager duty: SRE oncall (Priya) acknowledged. Observed node-level alerts: kubelet_eviction_count rising, node_restarts.
- 02:15: SRE console: netfilter conntrack errors and kernel logs showing "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" on nodes in pool-a and pool-b.
- 02:18: Control-plane metrics show elevated etcd request latencies (p95 writes > 400ms) coinciding with automated snapshot job starting at 02:14.
- 02:22: Mitigation step 1 applied: rate-limit and pause for the CI load-test job (kube job scaled down) and throttle internal healthchecks. 5xxs reduced but evictions continued.
- 02:25: Immediate mitigation step 2: Manually increase sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on impacted nodes via SSH + daemonset patch to apply temporarily to remaining nodes. Conntrack free count increased.
- 02:31: Node-level evictions drop; control-plane latency remains higher than baseline.
- 02:46: etcd snapshot job finished; control-plane latency returned to normal; cluster stabilized.
- 02:50: Post-mitigation monitoring indicated full recovery; incident declared mitigated at 02:56.

Root cause analysis (concise):
1) Immediate trigger: Burst of high-cardinality short-lived TCP flows from a misconfigured internal CI load-test job that spawned many concurrent ephemeral client connections (source: CI namespace). Those clients used short connection lifetimes and aggressive reconnects which produced large conntrack pressure.
2) Exposure: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max default value on our instance types was set conservatively for memory usage and did not accommodate the ephemeral connection pattern.
3) Amplification: An automated etcd snapshot job started concurrently and increased control-plane write latency. Slower API server responses increased pod dns and kubelet churn, leading to more retries and reconnects (feedback loop).
4) Missing guardrails: No per-namespace egress connection rate-limits for non-prod namespaces and insufficient CI isolation for network-heavy tests.

Why this was not prevented by existing alerts:
- We had node-level kernel log scraping but no high-cardinality conntrack-specific metric alert tuned to our traffic profile.
- The scheduled etcd snapshot is a heavier IO operation but was running in peak window; we lack a coordination policy that avoids heavy control-plane maintenance during known CI traffic windows.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Scaled the offending CI load-test down and paused its schedule (owner: Platform QA).
- Applied a temporary cluster-wide increase to net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max via one-off DaemonSet that writes sysctl on boot for remaining unaffected nodes (owner: SRE oncall).
- Throttled internal health-checks using the discovery service feature flag to reduce open connections from internal agents (owner: DevEx).
- Rolled out a kube-proxy config tweak to reduce conntrack timeout for CLOSED entries from 60s -> 30s in a canary pool to decrease table retention (owner: Networking eng).

Long-term remediation (proposed):
- Short-term (<= 2 weeks):
  - Increase default nf_conntrack_max for our instance classes in the node image (PR open).
  - Add a conntrack saturation alert with a severity that paginates when free entries < 10% for 5m.
  - Add a scheduled window guard to avoid heavy etcd maintenance (snapshots) coinciding with CI peak periods.
- Medium-term (2–8 weeks):
  - Implement per-namespace egress connection rate-limits via CNI policies or eBPF-based shaping for non-prod namespaces.
  - Harden CI load-test job templates to include connection pooling and to respect cluster egress budgets.
  - Tune kube-proxy / conntrack timeout defaults per workload class.
- Long-term (8–16 weeks):
  - Explore conntrack offload or leveraging scalable CNI (e.g., BPF datapath) to reduce kernel conntrack pressure.
  - Evaluate central throttling gateway for noisy internal clients with token-bucket rate control.

Runbook draft updates (changes to /runbooks/k8s-networking-conntrack.md):
- New play: "Conntrack saturation — fast triage" (add to top):
  1) Check kernel logs for "nf_conntrack: table full" on nodes (journalctl -k -u kubelet).
  2) Run: sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count && sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
  3) Identify top talkers: sudo ss -tunp | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 20
  4) If traffic originates from a specific namespace, scale down that workload and add network policy egress deny until stable.
  5) Temporary mitigation: apply daemonset that sets net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=VALUE (use conservative increase + 20%) and monitor.
  6) If evictions are widespread, consider cordoning the most affected nodes and migrating critical pods to canary pool with higher conntrack settings.
- Add checklist for coordinating control-plane maintenance with load windows.
- Add example kubectl/ssh commands and playbook snippets (copyable).

Action items and owners (with due dates):
- SRE: Deploy conntrack alert (JIRA-OPS-721) — due 2024-11-14 — Owner: Eli Navarro.
- Platform: Patch node image to increase nf_conntrack_max for c6i/c5 nodes (gitlab MR 492) — due 2024-11-21 — Owner: Marco Chen.
- DevEx: Harden CI load-test templates (add connection pooling guidance + egress budget) — due 2024-11-18 — Owner: Sofia Alvarez.
- Networking: Runbook update and kube-proxy timeout tuning RFC — due 2024-11-25 — Owner: Kunal Iyer.
- SRE/Platform: Build maintenance window policy for etcd snapshots to avoid CI peak — due 2024-12-01 — Owner: Priya Shah.

Post-incident notes / learnings:
- Conntrack pressure can be silently amplified by control-plane slowness; treat control-plane maintenance windows as first-class constraints for noisy workloads.
- Small adjustments to kernel defaults bought immediate relief but do not replace rate-limiting noisy clients.
- We need better non-prod traffic isolation to avoid noisy CI impacting prod-like services running in the same cluster.

Appendix: Quick commands used during mitigation:
- Check conntrack usage: cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count && cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
- Temporary set (one-off via daemonset): sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
- Identify top source IPs for connections: ss -antp | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 30
- Kube events for evictions: kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=Evicted -o wide --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

Status: Draft postmortem. Contents reviewed with oncall and owners. Next: finalize after remediation PRs merge and perform a follow-up verification run during controlled CI load in a canary cluster.

Prepared by: Priya Shah (SRE oncall).
